transcript:
Meeting: BlueHollow implementation immersion & runtime handshake
Date: 2026-11-07 15:00 PT | Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Priya S (Redwood CSM), Ethan M (Redwood SE), Jules P (Redwood Platform Eng), Marta R (BlueHollow Head ML Platforms), Tom B (Infra Lead), Anika P (Security), Liam O (PM)

Auto-summary: quick intro, state of current infra (on-prem + cloud hybrid), BlueHollow wants private deployment with VPC peering for pilot; security team wants KMS + audit logs + SSO; discussed telemetry and cost monitoring, proposed next steps and action items.

00:00 Priya S: Hey everyone, thanks for making time — quick intro, I'm Priya from Redwood CS, this is Ethan who will be SE and Jules who will help with runtime config. Marta, do you want to kick off with current state?
00:18 Marta R: Yeah thanks. So, hi — BlueHollow we run a hybrid infra, some workloads on AWS and a small on-prem cluster. Our immediate goal is a pilot for LLM assistants inside product search and support triage, so low RPS but need predictable latency and strong audit trails. We're leaning toward private deployment to keep data in our VPC.
00:40 Ethan M: Gotcha. When you say predictable latency, are you expecting sub-200ms token latency? Or is the SLO looser for the first pilot?
00:51 Tom B: For the pilot we can accept 200-400ms per token, but sustained p95 under 500ms is a requirement for UX. Also, network egress between our VPC and Redwood's control plane has to be minimal — we prefer peering and private endpoints.
01:12 Jules P: That aligns with what Private mode supports — a private control plane with customer-managed networking. There might be a brief tunnel for metrics if you want Redwood observability. We can run the entire inference in your VPC or in a dedicated pool in our region with secure routing.
01:29 Anika P: Security quick note: we need to see KMS integration for key management, audit logs forwarded to our SIEM, and SAML SSO for user access. Also retention settings for logs and model artefacts — we have an internal policy to keep traces for 90 days.
01:46 Priya S: Noted. We'll include the SOC2 artifacts and the KMS integration pattern. We have an enterprise package that supports HSM/KMS + audit log forwarding. We'll send the compliance pack after this call.
01:58 Marta R: Great. On the runtime side, we're curious about model pinning and rollback. We'll likely pin to a quantized variant for cost, but need a safe rollback path if quality degrades.
02:12 Ethan M: Yes, rollout and model versioning are supported. We can do canary rollouts with traffic split and automatic fallback to a baseline model. One caveat: quantized variants sometimes shift token output slightly; we recommend running a small eval set during the pilot to ensure QA thresholds are met.
02:30 Liam O: For evaluation, can you host eval harness or do we run locally?
02:36 Ethan M: We can host a preflight eval in the staging tenant and provide the eval harness — you run your test vectors against the pinned model and we produce quality diffs and token breakdowns.
02:48 Tom B: Network details — what ports/protocols do you need? We prefer not to open a broad range.
02:55 Jules P: We require outbound HTTPS to the control plane on TLS endpoints plus a couple of internal ports if you're doing peered GPU hosting; but for Private VPC deployment inside your subnet, we actually avoid egress — the control plane communicates over a customer-initiated tunnel only for control signals. We'll send a trimmed VPC checklist.
03:18 (Short crosstalk)
03:28 Marta R: On costs — we need a budget estimate for pilot: expected token volume low, but we want to see a clear delta between hosted and dedicated options so we can plan longer term.
03:40 Priya S: We'll produce a pilot pricing estimate with candidate configurations: hosted API (fastest to test), private single-tenant pool in your VPC (higher opex), and dedicated reserved capacity (if you want predictable commit). We'll attach unit cost per 1k tokens and rough infra estimates.
03:57 Anika P: Also data residency: some PII fields will be redacted by our preprocessor so not sent to Redwood, but we still want assurance on logs and encryption at rest.
04:10 Ethan M: Understood. We support encryption at rest, KMS integration, and configurable retention. For preprocessor redaction that's fine — we can also enable prefix caching options that respect PII masks.
04:26 Marta R: Good. Let's talk timeline: we want pilot live in staging by end of month — is that feasible?
04:34 Ethan M: Tight but doable if we get VPC details and the SSO/KMS requirements this week. Jules will own runtime config. Priya will coordinate docs and next steps.
04:44 Priya S: I'll send a short onboarding runbook post-call with checklist items and owners.
04:49 (short silence)
05:05 Transcript fragment — misc notes and clarifications follow, some transcription glitches likely:
05:12 Ethan M: (00:05:12) So the plan for the staging tenant — we spin up a small GPU pool, pin a 7B-quant model for throughput, set the batcher to a conservative 8 token batch, enable KV cache and prefix caching for repeated prompts, and add eval hooks.
05:33 Tom B: (00:05:33) Does Redwood's runtime support our on-prem GPU nodes? We have a small fleet with older Ampere cards — not sure about compute compatibility.
05:45 Jules P: (00:05:45) Yes, Private can run on-prem if you can run the Redwood runtime with our connector; compatibility depends on driver/kernel versions. We have a short compatibility matrix — I'll drop that link. Note: quantization paths vary by arch, so perf numbers can change.
06:07 Marta R: (00:06:07) We heard about auto-fallback — if GPU capacity is saturated, can traffic route to a hosted fallback? We need that during burn-in.
06:18 Ethan M: (00:06:18) Yes, smart routing supports fallback policies — you'll need to opt-in. There is a latency and cost delta but it's automated. We can also do regional fallback.
06:30 Anika P: (00:06:30) For audit logs, do you send full prompt text to Redwood logs? Our default is to redact or token-hash prompts.
06:39 Priya S: (00:06:39) We support configurable log capture. For PII sensitive prompts we recommend hashing or storing minimal metadata and forwarding structured telemetry into your SIEM. We'll show the log schema.
06:54 Liam O: (00:06:54) Who is the single point of contact for infra during the pilot?
06:58 Tom B: (00:06:58) I'll be engineering contact for infra, Marta will run the ML/quality signoffs, Anika is security.
07:05 Priya S: (00:07:05) Great. Quick risks: onboarding time if on-prem driver mismatch, quantized quality regressions, and network policy approvals. We'll highlight mitigations in the runbook.
07:20 (sound of link being pasted)
07:28 Ethan M: (00:07:28) I'll attach the compatibility matrix, a short staging run plan, and a mini-benchmark template. We recommend you run perf probes with the same sequence length distribution you expect in production — especially for search dialogs where tokens spike.
07:47 Marta R: (00:07:47) Sequence length — our median is 80 tokens, tail up to 600 for long threads. Does that change kernel selection?
07:56 Jules P: (00:07:56) Yes tail behavior matters. Runtime will choose kernels and batching heuristics differently; we'll tune batcher and KV retention. Longer tails increase memory footprint so we may recommend a larger instance type for the pilot to get realistic p95.
08:14 Tom B: (00:08:14) For the VPC peering, we prefer AWS PrivateLink style endpoints. Is that supported?
08:22 Ethan M: (00:08:22) We support PrivateLink and VPC peering, plus AWS Transit Gateway in larger setups. We'll document IP ranges and a minimal set of security group rules.
08:34 Anika P: (00:08:34) Regarding compliance evidence — we will need SOC 2 Type II, encryption in transit, and a third-party pentest summary. Can you provide those?
08:45 Priya S: (00:08:45) Yes, we'll share our SOC 2 pack, last pentest summary, and the KMS integration guide. Expect that in the post-call pack.
08:56 Marta R: (00:08:56) For success criteria — what metric set should we agree on at pilot end? We propose: p95 latency < 500ms, quality delta vs baseline < 3% on our eval, and error rate < 0.5%.
09:10 Ethan M: (00:09:10) Sounds reasonable. We'll help instrument key metrics and provide cost-per-1k-token breakdowns.
09:18 (brief cross talk)
09:35 Wrap / recap segment:
09:36 Priya S: Ok to recap — Priya will send runbook + compliance pack; Ethan will provision staging tenant and attach the benchmark harness; Jules will share runtime compatibility matrix; Tom will provide VPC CIDR and peering constraints; Anika will circulate compliance artifact list. We will aim for staging pilot by 11/30 and preliminary perf numbers in two weeks of the tenant being live.
09:58 Marta R: Confirmed, and we'll triage our internal approvals to meet that timeline.
10:06 Priya S: Next steps in chat, will follow up with calendar invites for security deep-dive and infra handoff.
10:14 (meeting closes)

Notes: transcription contains occasional mis-hearings: 'KV cache' sometimes transcribed as 'kayvee cash', 'Private control plane' as 'private control plain' etc. Action items listed above. Attachments referenced: (1) onboarding runbook link (post-call) (2) compatibility matrix (Ethan) (3) mini-benchmark template (Ethan) (4) SOC2/compliance pack (Priya)

End of transcript.
